From the first equation  

\[
s+\frac1p=8\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad s=8-\frac1p. \tag{2}
\]

From the second equation  

\[
p+\frac{s}{p}= \frac{25}{2}. \tag{3}
\]

Substituting (2) into (3),

\[
p+\frac{8-\frac1p}{p}= \frac{25}{2}
\Longrightarrow
p+\frac{8}{p}-\frac1{p^{2}}=\frac{25}{2}.
\]

Multiplying by \(2p^{2}\) gives the cubic

\[
2p^{3}-25p^{2}+16p-2=0.
\]

It factors as  

\[
2(p-\tfrac12)(p^{2}-12p+2)=0,
\]

so (since \(u,v>1\))  

\[
p=6+\sqrt{34}.
\]

Now from (2),

\[
s=8-\frac{1}{p}
    =8-\frac{6-\sqrt{34}}{2}
    =\frac{10+\sqrt{34}}{2}.
\]

Thus  

\[
u+v=\frac{10+\sqrt{34}}{2},\qquad
uv=6+\sqrt{34}. \tag{4}
\]

---

### 2.  Find the individual values of \(u\) and \(v\)

\(u\) and \(v\) are the roots of  

\[
t^{2}-st+p=0.
\]

Its discriminant is  

\[
\Delta=s^{2}-4p
      =\frac{19}{2}+\sqrt{34}
      =\Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt{34}}{2}\Bigr)^{2}.
\]

Hence  

\[
\sqrt\Delta = 1+\frac{\sqrt{34}}{2}.
\]

The two roots are  

\[
t=\frac{s\pm\sqrt\Delta}{2}
   =\frac{\displaystyle\frac{10+\sqrt{34}}{2}\pm
          \Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt{34}}{2}\Bigr)}{2}.
\]

Therefore  

\[
t=\;2\qquad\text{or}\qquad t=\frac{6+\sqrt{34}}{2}.
\]

Consequently \(\{u,v\}=\Bigl\{2,\; \dfrac{6+\sqrt{34}}{2}\Bigr\}\).

Since the problem asks for \(\log_y z=v\) and requests a non‑rational expression of the form \(\dfrac{a+\sqrt b}{c}\) with \(b\) square‑free, we must take the irrational value

\[
\log_y z=\frac{6+\sqrt{34}}{2}.
\]

Thus \(a=6,\; b=34,\; c=2\) and  

\[
a+b+c=6+34+2=42.
\]

\boxed{42}
